snippet.title: Backpacking for the first time | Packing, Prepping, & hiking!
snippet.description:
Hey Everyone!!

Join me on my first ever backpacking trip. I’ve done a couple hikes in my day and some camping as well but never both. This is my first overnight hike that I’ve ever done and it was awesome. In this video I will show you how I prepped and how it went!! 

We hiked Panorama Ridge which is about 30km and took a little detour to garabaldi lake which added about 4km to the total trip (very worth it). This is definetly my favorite hike and the views are absolutely stunning. 

It was such an awesome trip and i’m so lucky I got to experience it with my friends. I will definetly be doing this more in the future. 

I really hope you guys enjoy the video!!

- Kate

snippet.title: How Long the U S  Power Grid Can Actually Last — According to Their Own Reports
snippet.description:
How long can the U.S. power grid actually survive a major blackout? Not days — and the real answer is buried in the government's own reports.

In this video we break down just how fragile the American power grid really is, using the published findings of NERC, the U.S. Department of Energy, FERC, and the GAO. No fearmongering. No guessing. Just what their own official reports actually say, why almost nobody talks about it, and exactly what it means for you when the lights go out and don't come back.

What you'll walk away knowing:


Why more than 90% of all the power you use depends on a handful of aging machines you've never once noticed
The NERC forecast that now puts roughly half the United States at high risk of blackouts
How AI and data centers are quietly draining the grid faster than anyone can build new power to feed it
The custom-built part that can take up to two years to replace — and why there is no real national spare
The leaked federal estimate of how a coordinated failure could keep the country dark for 18 months or more
How a few sagging power lines cascaded into the 2003 blackout that hit 45 million people in minutes
The simple, realistic steps that put you ahead of 99% of people the moment the grid actually fails


Whether you're a prepper, a survivalist, or just someone who finally wants to understand the one system that every other system depends on, this breakdown is for you. By the end, you'll know something almost nobody around you knows: your own recovery time.

Subscribe to Fallout Raccoon for survival breakdowns the rest of the internet is too comfortable to make.


SOURCES & REFERENCES


NERC — 2025 Long-Term Reliability Assessment (North American Electric Reliability Corporation)
U.S. Department of Energy / Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory — 2024 Report on United States Data Center Energy Use (Congressionally mandated)
U.S. Department of Energy — Large Power Transformers and the U.S. Electric Grid
U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) — reporting on grid resilience and large power transformer spare reserves
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) — internal grid vulnerability analysis on critical substations (as reported by The Wall Street Journal)
U.S.–Canada Power System Outage Task Force — Final Report on the August 2003 Northeast Blackout
Metcalf substation attack, 2013 — public investigative reporting
Northern Virginia data center grid disconnection event, July 2024 — reported regional grid incident


This video is for educational and preparedness purposes only.

snippet.title: Global National: Aug. 9, 2026 | Evacuation zone expands as BC wildfires display extreme behaviour
snippet.description:
The wildfires raging in B.C.’s Interior have forced more than 20,000 people from their homes and the province’s wildfire service says the Bald Range wildfire near Summerland is displaying extreme fire behaviour. Shifting winds could also fuel the flames. The RCMP are working to confirm at least one reported death and the province, which remains under a state of emergency, says there has been significant structural loss. The federal government is stepping in to provide shelter and accommodations as the evacuation zone expands. Sarah MacDonald reports.

The Summerland, B.C., area is an agricultural hub in the Okanagan Valley, home to farms with livestock. Many animals need rescuing as the wildfires expand. Travis Persaud reports on the logistical challenge and the volunteers stepping up to help.
 
Typhoon Dolphin has now made landfall on China’s east coast, with torrential rain and winds of more than 150/km/h. Hundreds of thousands of people have evacuated across eastern China and more than 1,300 flights have been cancelled. Some areas are expecting more than 400mm of rain over the next few days. Authorities are warning of extreme flooding and landslides.
 
It’s been a summer of extreme weather across Canada and one Indigenous-led non-profit is helping First Nations to prepare for the worst. As Melissa Ridgen reports, communities are combining new technology with traditional knowledge to reduce the risks.

snippet.title: 18 Years Living Off-Grid on a Remote Island in a Solo-Built House & Homestead
snippet.description:
Tim Coertze has been living off-grid on a remote island in the Straight of Georgia (in Canada) for 18 years.  He is solo building his own retirement home using local materials from his own land, like rock, sand, and wood, as well as concrete for the foundation, rockwool for the insulation and tin for the roof.  He generates electricity with solar panels, he collects rainwater from his roof, he heats his home with firewood that he cuts down himself, and burns it in three different wood stoves: a monolithic masonry stove, a cast iron wood stove, or a rocket stove under his bathtub.  He also grows a lot of his own fruits and vegetables, sprouts seeds, bakes bread, and is raising a pair of Thai river water buffalo for milk.

You can follow Tim on his new YouTube channel here:
https://www.youtube.com/@timcoertze 

The island where Tim lives is completely off-grid, and can only be accessed by a pedestrian ferry (there is no car ferry), which makes it difficult to bring materials onto the island unless you can do it by barge, which is very expensive.  There is a community on the island so Tim finds that he can barter and trade with folks on the island for most of his needs, but he does go to town off island every couple of months to get groceries like coffee.

He does use propane to heat hot water and to cook when his wood stove is damped down, or when the wildfire risk is too high to burn a fire.

Tim is a thoughtful and talented creative builder who has done a ton of research into alternative building methods and systems from around the world, while focusing on using local materials, skills, and items for his projects.

One of his first jobs in the '80s was working at sea, where he saw floating garbage islands that forever changed the course of his life.  This led him to resign from his job and to seek out a remote and clean place where he could have a family, and live closer to the land.  He has been growing his own food and processing his own firewood for 40 years, and he now has grandchildren, so he managed to make his dreams a reality.  

But the experience of seeing those garbage islands never left him, and he has made an effort to manage his own waste on his land.  He keeps all of the garbage that he creates and sequesters it in the walls of his outbuildings, where they will be enclosed in concrete or plaster.  This reduces the energy needed to transport the garbage off the island and to a dump or recycling plant where only a fraction of the items will be recycled.  He has also repurposed the tires from his island truck as the chamber for his composting toilet.  He has managed to sequester 7 years of garbage in the walls of his solar panel shed.

He is not yet retired, and still works as a roofer, although he is hoping to spend less time doing the heavy work and more time managing crews moving forward.  He also plans to slowly complete his house with trim, paint, etc. and spend more time growing food once the house is complete.

This off-grid lifestyle can be challenging but Tim appreciates the silence, the satisfaction of being self sufficient, and the connection to the environment that allows him to appreciate the sun, the rain, and the plants around him.

A big thank you to Tim for sharing his story with us!

Thanks for watching!

snippet.description:
Loki Season 2 (2023) is essential Doomsday prep content. It answers what happened after Sylvie killed He Who Remains at the end of Season 1 and sets up the entire Multiverse Saga. Here is the complete 6-episode recap.

Episode 1 — Ouroboros:

The Sacred Timeline is splintering into infinite branches after Sylvie killed He Who Remains. Loki is time-slipping uncontrollably, jumping between the TVA’s past and future. He meets Ouroboros (OB), the TVA’s Repairs and Advancement worker played by Ke Huy Quan. OB helps Loki understand his time-slipping and reveals that the Temporal Loom, the machine that weaves the Sacred Timeline together, is overloading from too many branches.

Episode 2 — Breaking Brad:

The team locates Sylvie in 1982 Oklahoma, where she is living a normal life at a McDonald’s. She refuses to return to the TVA. Brad Wolfe (Rafael Casal), a TVA hunter, is revealed to actually be a Variant of a Hollywood movie star. Ravonna Renslayer is confirmed as an ongoing threat working against Mobius and the TVA.

Episode 3 — 1893:

The team travels to the 1893 Chicago World’s Fair. They find Victor Timely (Jonathan Majors), a stuttering, awkward inventor Variant of He Who Remains. Timely is essentially a proto-Kang. The team needs him to help stabilize the Temporal Loom.

Episode 4 — Heart of the TVA:

Ravonna Renslayer and Miss Minutes betray the team by working together to kill Victor Timely. Sylvie confronts Ravonna in a brutal fight. The Temporal Loom continues to overload dangerously.

Episode 5 — Science/Fiction:

snippet.title: High Protein Broccoli Paneer Kebabs Meal Prep ✨💚
snippet.description:
Meal Prep Paneer Broccoli Kebabs 🌱🧀

Ingredients:

•  Broccoli – 150g
•  Potatoes – 100g
•  Peas – 100g
•  Paneer – 150g
•  Salt
•  Black pepper
•  Chaat masala
•  Coriander powder
•  Roasted jeera powder
•  Saunf
•  Fresh coriander, chopped
•  Green chillies
•  Ginger-garlic paste

Prep:

1.  Steam broccoli, potatoes, and peas together for 10–15 mins or until soft.
2.  Mash everything together and add crumbled paneer.
3.  Mix in all the spices, fresh coriander, green chillies, and ginger-garlic paste.
4.  Shape into round kebabs.
5.  Place in a butter paper lined container to avoid sticking.
6.  Vacuum seal and freeze for meal prep.

Air Fry:
Spray lightly with sesame oil and air fry at 180°C for 15–18 mins.

To Cook Later:
Shallow cook in light oil on both sides until golden or air fry until crisp ✨
